partners.diseaseBName: neurodevelopmental disorder with visual defects and brain anomalies
partners.mechanism_chain: HK1 (HGNC:4922) —DISRUPTS→ Glucose-6-phosphate (CHEBI:17188); Glucose-6-phosphate (CHEBI:17188) —LEADS_TO→ Glycolysis (GO:0006096); Glycolysis (GO:0006096) —DECREASES→ Peripheral neuropathy (HP:0003198); Glycolysis (GO:0006096) —DECREASES→ Global developmental delay (HP:0001263); Glycolysis (GO:0006096) —DECREASES→ Cerebral atrophy (HP:0002094); Glycolysis (GO:0006096) —DECREASES→ Optic nerve atrophy (HP:0000703). Loss-of-function mutations in HK1 impair the first step of glycolysis, leading to reduced ATP production and altered metabolite flux. This impacts overall cellular energy homeostasis, which is particularly critical for highly energy-dependent cells like neurons. The downstream consequences manifest as peripheral neuropathy in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 4G, and global developmental delay, cerebral atrophy, and optic nerve atrophy in neurodevelopmental disorder with visual defects and brain anomalies.

partners.diseaseBName: muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy (congenital with intellectual disability), type B14

**Why it matters:** Understanding this overlap could reveal therapeutic targets that modulate glycosylation processes, potentially benefiting patients with either disease by improving protein function and cellular homeostasis.
